reason: This passage establishes a covenant between God and the entire people of Israel collectively, describing them all as destined to become 'a kingdom of priests' (Exodus 19:6). The text presents this elevated status as offered to the whole nation, not to an elite within it. Furthermore, the passage demonstrates that moral standing and accountability before God are not differentiated by elite status: Aaron, despite his special role as Moses' brother and later authority, commits a grave sin in the golden calf incident, showing that hierarchical position does not confer inherent superiority. The text emphasizes collective moral responsibility and equal covenantal standing, contradicting any notion that an elite class is inherently better than regular people.
